name: Sergeant Eddison

facts.text: Every named of the Hall takes no damage once drawn past its tether, and walks back to its post.

story:
The roster. Sergeant Eddison kept the duty roster of the Pennine watch and knew every man's post by heart, which is why the corruption kept him nearest the middle of the hall: a dead watch still needs someone to know where everyone stands. When the wizard asked for the watch to be doubled, it was Eddison who drew up the new roster in a single night. Like every officer of the Pennine watch, it is bound to its post: one step past where its captain stood it, no blow lands and it walks home at full health. Fight it where it stands. 

He walks between the posts as he did in life, checking, counting, and he raises the alarm when he finds a stranger where a watchman ought to be. Every raid in the hall is, to Eddison, an error in the roster. The bards say he still carries the doubled roster he drew up for the wizard, folded in his tunic, and that if you could read it you would see every post the corruption bound, and every name, and at the bottom, in a different hand, the names of the visitors the wizard expected.

Eddison counted the watch every morning at dawn, man by man, post by post, and the count was always right. On the last morning, the clerk wrote, the count came out one over: one more figure at the posts than there were men in the hall. Eddison counted three times. The extra one was never found. Eddison still counts, and the old hands say the count is still one over.
legend: Another five-thousand-health sergeant, but he sits in the middle of the hall, so pull him carefully or you wake the posts around him; take the posts nearest him first. Kill him where he stands; dragged off his post he cannot be hurt. Old hands say he raises the alarm to the nearest officers if left fighting long, so a quick kill matters more here than anywhere else in the hall. If your raid wakes the middle of the hall, fight your way out to the stair rather than stand in the open; the posts converge on the middle. Count your raid after.

aggro: You are not on the roster.

loremasterTopic.text: Sergeant Eddison kept the duty roster of the watch and knew every man's post by heart, which is why the corruption kept him nearest the middle of the Hall: a dead watch still needs someone to know where everyone stands.

bookPage: Sergeant Eddison drew up the doubled roster in a single night, as Master Aidon asked. Every man has two posts now, and some three, and Eddison knows them all by heart. He brought the roster to Lord Gildas this morning, and Lord Gildas signed it, and then the wizard asked to see it and wrote something at the bottom in his own hand and gave it back. Eddison showed me afterwards. The wizard had written a list of names. None of them is a man of the watch. When I asked Eddison who they were, he said they were the visitors, and folded it away.
